questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving objects — destructuring.
questions.explanation: Destructuring binds a to 3394 and b to 3 by matching property names, so their sum is 3397. Order in the pattern does not matter for objects. Carrying the operation through gives 3397; common slips include using only the first destructured field and using only the second field.
questions.hint: Object destructuring matches by property name.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving arrays — spread.

answer.exemplar: The spread expands the two existing entries and the trailing value is appended, giving 3 elements. The spread form creates a fresh array rather than mutating arr. The result is 3.

questions.explanation: The spread expands the two existing entries and the trailing value is appended, giving 3 elements. The spread form creates a fresh array rather than mutating arr. A complete answer names 3 and justifies it from the code rather than guessing.
questions.hint: Spread copies existing items before the new one is added.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving functions — rest.
questions.explanation: The rest parameter gathers every argument after the named one into an array, holding 2, 3 and 4, so its length is three. The leading value 3396 is bound to first. The printed value is 3, while the alternatives come from counting all arguments including first, counting only the last argument and assuming rest parameters collect nothing.
questions.hint: Rest collects arguments left after the fixed parameters.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving functions — hoisting.
questions.explanation: Function declarations are hoisted with their bodies, so typeof reports 'function' even before the source line. Their value is available throughout the enclosing scope. The printed value is function, while the alternatives come from assuming declarations are not hoisted, expecting the return value instead and thinking the early reference throws.
questions.hint: Declarations, unlike expressions, are initialized during hoisting.

questions.subject: JAVASCRIPT
questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving functions — closures.

options.misconception: Assuming the closure resets each call

questions.explanation: The closure keeps n alive between calls; the first invocation raises it to 3399 and the second to 3400. Each call mutates the same captured binding. The printed value is 3400, while the alternatives come from counting only the first increment, assuming the closure resets each call and counting three increments.
questions.hint: A closure retains the variable, it does not copy it per call.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret JavaScript behavior demonstrated by a short executable snippet involving functions — call binding.
questions.explanation: call explicitly sets this to obj, so get reads v and returns 3399. Without call, the detached function would not have obj as its receiver. Carrying the operation through gives 3399; common slips include assuming the detached function loses its value and guessing a default numeric result.
questions.hint: call supplies the receiver explicitly at invocation time.
